title: The Contractor Who Became an Employee
scenario_text: Everly Health's People Ops team is auditing headcount and tenure for a benefits-eligibility report. A discrepancy surfaces for a data engineer. Workday shows employee record E-55820, "Jonathan A. Pruitt," hire date 2023-09-05, worker type Regular (FTE), home email jon.pruitt@gmail.com, national ID (SSN) ending 4471. The prior contractor system (a Beeline VMS export) shows a contingent worker "John Pruitt" via staffing agency TalentBridge, assignment start 2022-02-14, assignment end 2023-09-01, worker type Contingent, personal email jon.pruitt@gmail.com, no SSN captured (agency-employed). Okta shows a single active user jpruitt@everlyhealth.com created 2022-02-16, with a profile attribute "employmentStatus" that flipped from "Contractor" to "Employee" on 2023-09-05. The Workday record's "prior service" field is blank. A Slack message from the hiring manager reads: "Jon's been with us on the data platform team since Feb 2022 as a contractor through TalentBridge; we converted him to FTE the day after his contract ended." Everly's benefits policy vests certain benefits based on continuous service, but contingent-worker time through a staffing agency does not count toward FTE benefits tenure; benefits tenure begins at the FTE conversion date. The audit question is strictly about benefits-eligibility tenure, not total time associated with the company.
question: What date should be used as the start of Jonathan Pruitt's benefits-eligibility tenure?
